Arthur Appel, de IBM, propuso en 1968 la: Arthur Appel, of IBM, proposed in 1968 firing one ray per pixel to find out what is seen. In 1980 Turner Whitted, at Bell Labs, added the idea that changed everything: when a ray hits a mirror or a glass, new bounced and refracted rays are fired, and so on. His image of two spheres on a chequerboard took hours to compute. For decades it was the cinema's technique, computed frame by frame on computer farms. In 2018 the first consumer graphics cards with circuits dedicated to tracing rays in real time arrived.
